# 2 Baruch Chapter 2 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 2:1 — "for a season shall it be forgotten"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "but-only for-a-season shall it-be-forgotten" | Preserves Syriac adversative and temporal phrase literally |
| LOGOS | "but only for a season shall it be forgotten" | Formal English, preserves structure |
| PNEUMA | "It is set aside only for a while" | "Set aside" for "forgotten"; "a while" for "a season" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "For a season" is the established rendering in Charles and Klijn. PNEUMA's "set aside" obscures the verb; "a while" is less specific.

---

## 2:4 — Eschatological reversal

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "those who-have-been-cast-down shall-be-lifted-up, and those who-have-been-lifted-up shall-be-cast-down" | Literal chiasm preserved with hyphenation |
| LOGOS | "Those who have been cast down shall be lifted up, and those who have been lifted up shall be cast down" | Formal, chiasm intact |
| PNEUMA | "Those who were brought low will be raised up, and those who were raised high will be brought low" | Active/passive shift; "brought low/raised high" |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. The passive construction ("cast down/lifted up") reflects the divine agency in the Syriac better than PNEUMA's active equivalents.

---

## 2:7 — "created the world for the sake of Israel"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-LORD created the-world for-the-sake-of-Israel" | Literal divine name and purpose clause |
| LOGOS | "the Lord created the world for the sake of Israel" | Standard formal rendering |
| PNEUMA | "The Lord made the world for Israel's sake" | "Made" for "created"; compressed genitive |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** LOGOS adopted. "Created" is theologically more precise than "made" — the Syriac verb here implies the bara'/creation register. "For the sake of Israel" preferred over compressed form.

---

**Total disagreements this chapter: 3**
